'''Ganugapati Sree Rama Subba Rao''' (born 21 August 1937) is an Indian natural product chemist and a former chair of the department of sciences at the [[Indian Institute of Science]] (IISc).<ref name="Accolades">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iisc.ac.in/research/accolades/indian-national-science-academy/ |title=Accolades |year=2016 |publisher=Indian Institute of Science}}</ref> He is known for his researches on "dihydroaromatics obtained through [[Birch reduction]] of aromatic compounds"<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=79 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |year=2016 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> and is an elected fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]],<ref name="Indian fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N87-0980 |title=Indian fellow |year=2016 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=20 November 2016 |archive-date=25 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210225014751/https://www.insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N87-0980 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Subba_Rao,_Prof._Ganugapati_Sree_Rama |title=Fellow profile |year=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1982, for his contributions to chemical sciences.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |year=2016 | access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref>

== Biography ==
[[File:IISc Main Building.jpg|thumb|235px|Indian Institute of Science]]
G. S. R. Subba Rao, born on 21 August 1937 in [[Kolavennu]], in the south Indian state of [[Andhra Pradesh]] to Satyanarayana Ganugapati and Lakshmi Subba Rao, did his college studies at [[Andhra University]] from where he graduated in chemistry in 1957 and followed it up with a master's degree in 1959.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> Subsequently, he enrolled for doctoral studies under the guidance of L. Ramachandra Row and secured the degree of Doctor of Science in 1962 and moved to [[University of Manchester]] for his post-doctoral studies at the laboratory of [[Arthur J. Birch]].<ref name="G.S.R. Subba Rao - Faculty profile">{{Cite web |url=http://orgchem.iisc.ernet.in/faculty/gsrs/gsrs.html |title=G.S.R. Subba Rao – Faculty profile |year=2016 |publisher=Indian Institute of Science}}</ref> He obtained a PhD in 1966 and completed his post doctoral studies at [[Australian National University]]. On his return to India in 1971, he joined the [[Indian Institute of Science]] as a member of faculty at the department of organic chemistry where he set up his research group and served as the dean of the faculty of science, eventually superannuating from academic duties as the chair of the department.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> He also serves as a director of Novosynth Research Labs<ref name="Novosynth Research Labs">{{Cite web |url=http://informix.in/novosynth_research_labs_private_limited_bangalore/894621/ |title=Novosynth Research Labs |year=2016 |publisher=InfoMix}}</ref> and Bal Research Foundation, two entities involved in scientific research.<ref name="Bal Research Foundation">{{Cite web |url=http://ecorpinfo.com/company/BAL-RESEARCH-FOUNDATION/U73100KA2014NPL076995 |title=Bal Research Foundation |year=2016 |publisher=eCorp Info}}</ref>

Subba Rao is married to Lakshmi Sita Valluri and the couple have two children, a daughter, Rama and son, Krishna. The family lives in [[Hyderabad]].<ref name="G.S.R. Subba Rao - Faculty profile" />

== Legacy ==
Subba Rao's early researches were focused on natural product chemistry and through his studies of the dihydroaromatics, he developed new protocols for synthesising aromatic compounds using [[Birch reduction]].<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | year=1999 | access-date=5 October 2016 | pages=34 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | archive-date=4 March 2016 | url-status=dead }}</ref> His contributions are reported in the synthesis of [[steroids]] and [[polyketides]] as well as the studies of the "mechanistic aspects of dissolving metal reductions". His work has been documented by way of over 150 articles published in peer-reviewed journals<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Subba_Rao=3AGanugapati_Sree_Rama=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |year=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> He has guided 28 doctoral scholars in their studies, has been associated with several journals as a member of their editorial boards and served as a council member of the Indian National Science Academy from 2001 to 2003.<ref name="Indian fellow" />

== Awards and honours ==
The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] awarded Subba Rao the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1982.<ref name="Chemical Sciences">{{cite web | url=http://www.csir.res.in/External/Heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | title=Chemical Sciences | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research |year=2016 | access-date=7 November 2016 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120912012851/http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | archive-date=12 September 2012 }}</ref> He received the Sir C. V. Raman Award of the [[University Grants Commission of India]] in 1992 and the T. R. Seshadri 70th Birthday Commemoration Medal of the Indian National Science Academy (INSA) in 1997.<ref name="Professor TR Seshadri 70th Birthday Commemoration Medal">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#ptr |title=Professor TR Seshadri 70th Birthday Commemoration Medal |year=2016 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=20 November 2016 |archive-date=16 September 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916233840/http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#ptr |url-status=dead }}</ref> INSA honoured him again with the Senior Scientist Award in 2003<ref name="Senior Scientist Award">{{Cite web |url=https://insaindia.res.in/name1.php |title=Recipients of INSA-Senior Scientists |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220112121310/https://www.insaindia.res.in/name1.php |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref> and the Golden Jubilee Commemoration Medal in 2004.<ref name="Golden Jubilee Commemoration Medal">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#910 |title=Golden Jubilee Commemoration Medal |year=2016 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=20 November 2016 |archive-date=16 September 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916233840/http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#910 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In between, he received the Alumni Award for Excellence in Research in Science of the Indian Institute of Science in 1998.<ref name="Alumni Award for Excellence in Research in Science">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iisc.ac.in/institute-awards/alumni-award-for-excellence-in-research-in-scienceengineering/ |title=Alumni Award for Excellence in Research in Science |year=2016 |publisher=Indian Institute of Science}}</ref> He is an elected fellow of the Indian National Science Academy and the Indian Academy of Sciences<ref name="Fellow profile" /> and has delivered a number of award orations including the Professor Venkataraman Memorial Lecture of the [[National Chemical Laboratory]].<ref name="Professor Venkataraman Memorial Lecture">{{Cite web |url=http://www.csir.res.in/csir/External/Heads/events/ncl20063.doc |title=Professor Venkataraman Memorial Lecture |year=2016 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research |access-date=20 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161120150418/http://www.csir.res.in/csir/External/Heads/events/ncl20063.doc |archive-date=20 November 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
